page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, utilizing 2 threads per core. System memory totals 4.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The configuration does not include local disk storage or integrated GPU accelerators, requiring attached network storage for persistent data. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmark analysis shows exceptional single-core processing capability paired with modest parallel capacity. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3111.68) and strong single-core Geekbench performance (1997.0). In contrast, total multi-core scalability is limited by the 2-vCPU count, resulting in weak multi-core Geekbench (2481.0) and PassMark CPU (3870.88) scores. Memory throughput exhibits average speeds for large uncached block reads (47.32 GB/sec) and writes (27.49 GB/sec), though small-block cached memory bandwidth scores low (153.15 GB/sec).

With its high clock-speed AMD EPYC core paired with a modest 4.0 GB memory footprint, ecs.c8ae.large offers qualitative resource efficiency for jobs that require raw single-threaded computing power without paying for excessive RAM allocations. Appropriate workload fits include lightweight single-threaded web applications, simple code compilation pipelines, static file utilities, and basic background processing workers. High-concurrency relational databases and parallel data analytics are constrained by the core count and memory bandwidth.

Configured with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps, the instance omits bundled local storage and GPUs. Supported CPU extensions include AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, securing top-tier stress-ng single-core scores (3111.68) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1997.0. Conversely, multi-core throughput and database operation metrics remain in lower performance tiers due to the 2-vCPU limit. Uncached memory bandwidth operates at average levels (47.32 GB/sec read, 27.49 GB/sec write). This server is suitable for lightweight single-threaded application hosting, basic code compilation, and small task processing.
